I've been writing down statements about mapping class groups of surfaces as challenges for LeanEval, and when I tried to construct the forward homomorphism Mod±(S)→Out(π1(S))\mathrm{Mod}^\pm(S)\to\mathrm{Out}(\pi_1(S))Mod±(S)→Out(π1​(S)), I discovered the following (2-)categorical construction:

Given a category C and an object X : C we may consider all endofunctors C ⥤ C that maps X to an isomorphic object, which form a submonoid, and it seems natural to call this the "stabilizer" of X. Every endofunctor F induces a homomorphism End X →* End F(X), and composing with conjugation by an isomorphism F(X) ≅ X produces an endomorphism of End X, which is independent of the choice of the isomorphism up to conjugation, i.e. when considered as an element in the outer endomorphism monoid OuterEnd (End X) := End (End X) ⧸ Inn (End X); note that the units in this monoid form the outer automorphism group Out (End X) := Aut (End X) ⧸ Inn (End X). It is straightforward to show that this defines a canonical homomorphism from the stabilizer of X to OuterEnd (End X), and moreover (naturally) isomorphic endofunctors induces the same outer endomorphism. This construction has been formalized in #44611 but probably can be generalized from Cat to an arbitrary 2-category.

Now let S be a topological space and x : S be a point considered as an object in FundamentalGroupoid S, then π1(S,x)\pi_1(S,x)π1​(S,x) is exactly (defined as) End x. Every continuous self-map of S induces an endofunctor on the fundamental groupoid, and homotopic maps induces naturally isomorphic ones. If S is path-connected then every induced endofunctor is in the stabilizer of x. The categorical construction then produces a homomorphism from the "mapping class monoid of S" (continuous self-maps up to homotopy) to OuterEnd (End x), which is the forward map on p.231 of *A Primer on Mapping Class Groups*:

As noted there, if S is a K(π,1) then this is an isomorphism. Consequently, the homomorphism from the units in the mapping class monoid (which are exactly homotopy self-equivalences up to homotopy) to Out (End X) is an isomorphism. Since the (extended) mapping class group is defined to consist of self-homeomorphisms up to isotopy, to prove Dehn–Nielsen–Baer theorem we are left to show that every homotopy self-equivalence is homotopic to a homeomorphism, and every two homotopic homeomorphisms are isotopic (see Theorem 1.12).
